passage:
Sunday, 9 June
Six months ago I made a list called 'Careers I'd like to steal': five people whose paths look like where I want to be in ten years. Two of them said yes to a monthly chat: Shreya, who went from testing to leading a platform team, and Mr Dsouza, who runs his own consultancy.
Today was my sixth chat with Shreya. I asked what actually mattered in her path. Not what I expected. She said the certification I'm studying for barely counted; what counted was volunteering, in year two, for the ugly migration project nobody wanted. Mr Dsouza said something similar last month about taking on client calls early.
So I'm changing the plan: dropping the second certification, and asking my lead for the next messy project instead.
Francis

qa.q: Who went from testing to leading a platform team?
How might Francis have felt hearing that the certification barely counted?
qa.a: Francis was probably surprised and a little deflated, but also relieved to learn what really matters before spending more time on it.

qa.q: What else could Francis do with what the mentors shared?
qa.a: Francis could check the advice against a third person's path and notice, over the next months, whether the messy project really builds the skills needed.

qa.q: How might Shreya see these monthly chats?
qa.a: Shreya may enjoy passing on real lessons and feel valued when Francis actually changes the plan.

grounding: It shows someone choosing role models, asking two for monthly chats, learning which choices mattered and adjusting the plan.

Bhupen: Hi Hansa ma'am, I'm Bhupen from the Guwahati office. I've followed your move from support to product for a while. Could I ask for 20 minutes a month for a few months? I'm trying to plan the next five years
Hansa: Happy to. First Saturday of the month, 10 am? Come with questions, not a CV 🙂
[Three months later]
Bhupen: thank you for today. the part about saying yes to customer calls early really stuck
Hansa: that choice mattered more than any course I did
Bhupen: I've changed my plan. asking my manager to put me on the customer call rotation from next month, and pushing the MBA idea back a year
Hansa: good. try it for a quarter, then tell me what you learnt
Bhupen: will do. same Saturday?
Hansa: same Saturday 👍

qa.q: When did Hansa offer to meet?
qa.a: The first Saturday of the month, at 10 am.

qa.q: How does Bhupen seem to feel after three months of chats?
qa.a: Bhupen seems grateful and motivated, excited enough by one lesson to change the plan.

qa.q: What would you advise Bhupen to do about the MBA idea?
qa.a: Keep it on the list but revisit it after a quarter of customer calls, when Bhupen knows more about what the product path needs.

qa.q: How might Hansa see Bhupen's request?
qa.a: Hansa likely appreciates a clear, respectful ask and enjoys seeing the advice actually used.

grounding: It shows someone reaching out to a person whose career looks appealing for monthly chats and adjusting the plan with that real experience.
